tldr: Links and the sidebar now carry only the namespace to a new screen, and keep every param on the same screen. The dashboard writes the active namespace into the URL after the API accepts it.
goal: Stop page-local params from following the user, and keep the namespace in the URL, so a refresh or a shared link opens the same namespace.

story.heading: buildScopedPath added: 1 rule for every in-app link
story.body: A new screen gets the namespace and the params the target names. The same screen keeps all params. It replaces 4 copies of merge-all.

story.heading: Namespaces now writes the namespace back to the URL
story.body: After /v1/context answers, NamespaceProvider puts the namespace in the URL with replaceState. An unreachable namespace becomes the one in use.

story.heading: The write-back keeps the screen loaded
story.body: useGetContext seeds the cache key of the resolved namespace. NamespaceProvider holds the last resolved state, so the loading gate stays closed.

story.heading: Back to sessions now keeps only the namespace
story.body: The session page calls push from useNamespacedNavigation. The params of the conversation stay on the session page.

story.heading: 8 requirements of url-param-scoping, all met
story.body: Navigation implements the 4 param rules. Namespaces implements the 4 rules for the namespace in the URL. Unit tests cover each scenario.

story.heading: The whole change
story.body: Navigation decides which params follow the user. Namespaces keeps the URL and the namespace in use the same. The change stays inside the dashboard.

components.summary: The session page goes back to the session history with the namespace only, not with the params of the conversation.
NamespacedLink, useNamespacedNavigation and the sidebar call buildScopedPath; only namespace follows the user to a new screen.
NamespaceProvider derives the namespace in render, writes it to the URL and drops setNamespace, createNamespace and availableNamespaces.

decisions.title: An allowlist of app-scoped params, not a denylist
decisions.why: The app reads 25 params and only namespace is app-scoped. A new param that nobody classifies stays page-local, so it cannot leak.
decisions.alternative: Use the denylist of session-params.ts for the whole app.

decisions.title: Scope by pathname, not by a declaration per screen
decisions.why: The same pathname means the same screen, which owns its params. No screen needs a config, and a target can name a param it needs.
decisions.alternative: A registry that maps each route to the params it holds.

decisions.title: replaceState with a query-only URL, not router.replace
decisions.why: router.replace makes a server round trip and can fetch twice on mount. A bare query keeps the base path that usePathname() does not include.
decisions.alternative: router.replace with the pathname from usePathname().

decisions.title: Derive the namespace in render
decisions.why: A useState('default') seed sent a request for the wrong namespace first. The state now comes from the /v1/context answer or its error.
decisions.alternative: Keep the namespace in useState and sync it in an effect.

decisions.title: Seed the context cache for the resolved namespace
decisions.why: The write-back selects a new query key. The seed serves it from the response in hand, so /v1/context is not fetched twice.
decisions.alternative: Let the new key fetch and show the loading gate again.
